item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Court to rule on Swedish citizens behind Denmark grenade attack, government to abolish F grade, migration minister to apply 'poor conduct' law retroactively and more news from Sweden on Tuesday.

item.title: How can you watch the 2026 Winter Olympics on Swedish TV?
item.description: The Winter Olympics kicks off in Milan and Cortina on Friday. In Sweden, it's arguably a bigger deal than the summer variety. Where can you follow the action on Swedish TV?

item.title: Swedish government wants to call MPs back to parliament from summer break
item.description: Sweden's government wants to call MPs back to parliament during the summer recess so that it can drive through the last remaining policies it agreed under the Tidö Agreement with the Sweden Democrats.

item.title: Why it could be easier to get on the Swedish housing ladder from April 1st
item.description: A new proposal set to come into force on April 1st will change the rules around mortgages, increasing accessibility for first-time buyers. But what exactly does it include?

item.title: What are the chances of the Sweden Democrats' leader becoming prime minister?
item.description: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson recently said in an interview with SVT that he’s ready to be prime minister. But what are the chances of that actually happening?

item.title: Sweden and Denmark pledge $290 million to Ukraine air defence
item.description: Sweden and Denmark announced on Tuesday that they plan to procure air defence systems worth 2.6 billion kronor ($290 million) for Ukraine, as the war-torn country struggles to fend off massive Russian bombardments.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: nja
item.description: This little word can help you navigate tricky social situations with ease in Swedish.

item.title: Politics in Sweden: Are Swedish politicians free to break the law now?
item.description: Can politicians simply refuse to follow Swedish law without facing any consequences? That’s the question being asked by the Migration Agency’s former chief after politicians in a southern town were cleared of wrongdoing despite refusing to house a family of refugees.

item.title: Two Swedes jailed in Denmark for attack on Israeli embassy
item.description: Two young Swedes were sentenced to jail terms on Tuesday for throwing grenades at Israel's embassy in Denmark over a year ago.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Swedish drinking water companies used Russian pump company, share of women on Swedish company boards hits record high, and other news from Sweden on Wednesday.
